section_summary: This section concerns the reconstruction, control and export of Japanese textiles in early 1947. Industry representatives press for limits on cotton mills and textile machinery, while State Department and occupation officials address sales, allocation, payment and shipping to overseas buyers. It also records a Malayan purchasing mission’s complaint about SCAP trade administration and arrangements for Turkish and Siamese missions to visit Japan.

subfiles.title: Cotton-Textile Institute proposals on Japanese textiles
subfiles.about: Industry representatives seek interim controls on Japanese textile production, machinery and exports.
subfiles.summary: Planz favors a five-year limit on cotton spindles and looms, controls on textile machinery, private export sales and world-level prices. He asks for information about Japanese rehabilitation proposals and a conference with State Department officials.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Planz letter
subfiles.about: State acknowledges the institute’s policy proposals and interest in a conference.
subfiles.summary: Thorp promises a fuller reply and notes the request for a conference.

subfiles.title: State reply on Japanese textile policy
subfiles.about: State discusses reconstruction limits and obstacles to private textile trading.
subfiles.summary: Thorp says limits remain under consideration and invites an industry meeting.

subfiles.title: Proposed reply and internal comments on Planz proposals
subfiles.about: Officials assess proposed Japanese textile restrictions and export arrangements.
subfiles.summary: The division favors a general written reply before discussing details at a conference. It reviews unsettled spindle limits, opposition to machinery export restrictions, barriers to private trading, yen loans for mill rehabilitation and the continuing need for U.S. Commercial Company sales.

subfiles.title: Offer of German and Japanese cotton textiles to Yemen
subfiles.to: Imam Yahya bin Mohammed bin Hamid ed Din
subfiles.about: USCC offers cotton cloth and yarn for Yemen’s anticipated import shortfall.
subfiles.summary: Gardiner asks Yemen to estimate requirements for dollar purchases.

subfiles.title: Cotton textile constructions and prices
subfiles.to: Imam Yahya bin Mohammed bin Hamid ed Din
subfiles.about: Lists available textile constructions, yarn counts and prices.
subfiles.summary: Tables detail fabrics and yarn offered with the Yemen letter.

subfiles.title: Siamese payment and shipping request
subfiles.about: Siam seeks more time to pay for Japanese textiles and economical return shipping.
subfiles.summary: Siam can pay $3 million initially but requests rice or other sales, or twelve months for the balance.

subfiles.title: Request for priority to import Japanese textiles
subfiles.about: A New York textile merchant asks for import priority.
subfiles.summary: Simon describes his business and asks how to obtain Japanese textiles.

subfiles.title: Cover letter forwarding Simon inquiry
subfiles.about: Simon asks State to forward his enclosed letter to the trade board.
subfiles.summary: Requests delivery of the enclosed inquiry.

subfiles.title: Reply to Simon on Japanese textile sales
subfiles.about: State explains allocations and directs Simon to USCC sales information.
subfiles.summary: Robinson identifies limited Far Eastern options and USCC’s New York display room.

subfiles.title: Publication of rayon and synthetic fiber report
subfiles.about: Rose arranges distribution of his study of Japan’s rayon industry.
subfiles.summary: Rose sends copies for State, SCAP and other offices and explains the report’s origin and availability.

subfiles.title: The Rayon and Synthetic Fiber Industry of Japan prospectus
subfiles.about: Promotional description and contents of Rose’s study.
subfiles.summary: The prospectus describes the Textile Mission’s research into Japanese rayon capacity, production, technology and trade, then lists the book’s chapters and ordering information.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Rose report copies
subfiles.about: Martin confirms receipt and forwarding of report copies.
subfiles.summary: Six copies are being sent to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Instruction to transmit Yemen textile offer
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Jidda
subfiles.about: State directs delivery of the USCC textile offer to Yemen’s ruler.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Gardiner’s memorandum for presentation to the Imam.

subfiles.title: Complimentary copies of Rose report
subfiles.about: The institute sends complimentary copies of Rose’s study.
subfiles.summary: Jacobs arranges one departmental copy and six for SCAP.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Jacobs
subfiles.about: Martin thanks Jacobs for complimentary report copies.
subfiles.summary: Copies arrived and six are being sent to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Turkish inquiry about Japanese textiles
subfiles.about: Turkey requests guidance on inquiries from textile importers.
subfiles.summary: The embassy asks how to handle prospective Japanese textile trade.

subfiles.title: Routing note on Turkish trade reply
subfiles.about: A draft reply explains channels for Japanese-Turkish trade inquiries.
subfiles.summary: Moreland recommends concurrence with the attached reply.

subfiles.title: Instructions on Japanese-Turkish trade
subfiles.from: John H. Hilldring, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: State explains permitted inquiries and government responsibility for trade.
subfiles.summary: Turkish buyers may inquire directly in Japan, while trade remains government sponsored. USCC handles all Japanese cotton textile sales.

subfiles.title: Record copy replacement notice
subfiles.about: Marks a replacement record copy of Tokyo despatch 868.
subfiles.summary: Directs return of the replacement copy for filing.

subfiles.title: Tokyo despatch on British textile purchasing protest, poor copy
subfiles.about: Forwards a Malayan mission’s protest about SCAP foreign trade administration.
subfiles.summary: The despatch encloses the protest, SCAP’s answer and an earlier silk-sample request.

subfiles.title: Malayan purchasing mission protest, poor copy
subfiles.about: The mission complains of delays and inadequate service by SCAP’s Foreign Trade Division.
subfiles.summary: Boyd cites unanswered letters, missing silk samples and unavailable wool prices. He says Malaya may buy elsewhere and proposes adding a British textile expert to SCAP’s staff.

subfiles.title: Marquat reply to purchasing mission, poor copy
subfiles.about: SCAP responds to complaints about textile trade administration.
subfiles.summary: Marquat attributes delays to workload, information checks and sample reinspection. He says replacement silk books have been sent and wool prices await Bradford quotations.

subfiles.title: Malayan request for silk samples, poor copy
subfiles.about: Boyd asks for the remaining silk samples to complete selections.
subfiles.summary: The mission reports a selection of 437,655 yards.

subfiles.title: File note on British protest
subfiles.about: A State official summarizes the Malayan complaint and Marquat’s response.
subfiles.summary: The note highlights criticism of delay and the unanswered proposal for a British expert.

subfiles.title: Tokyo despatch on British textile purchasing protest, clean copy
subfiles.about: Forwards the Malayan mission’s protest and related correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Bishop notes no formal British liaison protest or comparable complaint.

subfiles.title: Malayan purchasing mission protest, clean copy
subfiles.about: The mission protests delays in arranging Japanese textile purchases.
subfiles.summary: Boyd says the Foreign Trade Division lacks staff and market knowledge, has not answered requests, and has delayed silk samples and wool quotations. He seeks British intervention and a British commercial expert.

subfiles.title: Marquat reply to purchasing mission, clean copy
subfiles.about: SCAP explains delays in textile purchasing.
subfiles.summary: Marquat cites occupation trading controls, workload and verification needs. He says new silk sample books have been sent and wool quotations await prices from London.

subfiles.title: Malayan silk sample request, clean copy
subfiles.about: The mission requests returned silk samples.
subfiles.summary: Boyd seeks samples after selecting 437,655 yards of silk piece goods.

subfiles.title: Proposed sterling payment clause for British colonial purchases
subfiles.to: Secretaries of State, War and Agriculture
subfiles.about: USCC requests approval for a conditional sterling payment clause.
subfiles.summary: The Crown Agents propose a large forward purchase of Japanese fabrics and yarn. Henderson asks whether contracts may provide for sterling payment if the U.S. and U.K. governments later agree to it.

subfiles.title: Guidance on first-half 1947 Japanese textile allocations
subfiles.about: State sets a deadline for sales under proposed allocation guidelines.
subfiles.summary: USCC may sell outside the proposed allocation plan if contracts are not signed by March 1.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of allocation guidance
subfiles.about: Martin asks the trade board to circulate his letter to Gardiner.
subfiles.summary: Requests copies for board members and Gardiner.

subfiles.title: Withdrawal of request for sterling clause opinion
subfiles.about: State notes USCC no longer seeks an immediate opinion on a payment clause.
subfiles.summary: Martin reserves the effect on existing contracts for any future currency agreement.

subfiles.title: Siamese textile purchase difficulties
subfiles.about: Siam reports slow textile sales and asks about rice and shipping arrangements.
subfiles.summary: Siam can buy more textiles if Korean rice sales and economical transport are arranged.

subfiles.title: Philippine cable routing memorandum
subfiles.about: Ely seeks an inquiry into a canceled Philippine textile order.
subfiles.summary: He asks that the embassy avoid pressuring the Philippine government.

subfiles.title: USCC cover letter for Philippine cable draft
subfiles.about: Gardiner forwards a proposed cable about Philippine textile purchases.
subfiles.summary: Requests attention to the attached draft.

subfiles.title: Draft inquiry into Philippine textile purchases
subfiles.about: USCC seeks shipping plans and reasons for withdrawal of a further order.
subfiles.summary: The draft concerns 13.6 million yards under contract and a canceled 15-million-yard purchase.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Philippine cable request
subfiles.about: State confirms transmission of the proposed Manila message.
subfiles.summary: The department is sending the enclosed message to Manila.

subfiles.title: Draft acknowledgment of Turkish commission note
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Turkey’s proposed purchasing commission.
subfiles.summary: Names the three proposed commission members.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Turkish commission travel and security review
subfiles.about: Officials coordinate travel permission for three Turkish textile purchasers.
subfiles.summary: A records check flags Ragip Sipahi’s reported holdings for German and Belgian firms. The memorandum traces conflicting permit actions by State, War and Joint Chiefs offices and calls for further information before the mission travels.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Turkish commission departure
subfiles.about: Wolberg alerts the Turkish Embassy to required travel documentation.
subfiles.summary: She advises a required statement for the travelers awaiting a flight in San Francisco.

subfiles.title: Military clearance for Turkish travelers
subfiles.about: Joint Chiefs report no military objection to three Turks traveling to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Air priority and extra baggage are arranged.

subfiles.title: Receipt for classified Sipahi information
subfiles.about: Acknowledges a memorandum containing classified information on Sipahi.
subfiles.summary: Receipt covers classified Sipahi information.

subfiles.title: Turkish request to send a textile commission
subfiles.about: Turkey seeks assistance for a commission inspecting Japanese cotton purchases.
subfiles.summary: The note names Inan, Aydinelli and Sipahi and requests help with travel.

subfiles.title: Telegram record copy replacement notice
subfiles.about: Marks a replacement record copy for a telegram.
subfiles.summary: Directs return of the copy for filing.

subfiles.title: Siamese representatives seek entry to Japan
subfiles.about: Siam requests entry approval for two representatives arranging textile shipments.
subfiles.summary: Stanton also repeats unanswered questions about shipping.

subfiles.title: Rayon reports sent to Beale
subfiles.about: O’Brien sends textile mission and rayon reports after a tariff discussion.
subfiles.summary: Two reports supplement the discussion of rayon yarn tariffs.

subfiles.title: Beale acknowledgment of rayon reports
subfiles.about: Beale thanks O’Brien for reports and a meeting.
subfiles.summary: He may request further information.

subfiles.title: Conditional approval of Siamese mission
subfiles.about: State approves mission entry subject to SCAP concurrence.
subfiles.summary: SCAP will inform Bangkok directly.

subfiles.title: SCAP requests details on Siamese representatives
subfiles.to: American Minister, Bangkok; Secretary of State
subfiles.about: SCAP requests required personal details before granting entry.
subfiles.summary: No objection is foreseen, but Circular 8 information is required.

subfiles.title: Textile machinery industry capacity argument
subfiles.about: Machinery manufacturers press for deep limits on Japan’s textile machinery industry.
subfiles.summary: West argues Japan’s prewar machinery capacity was disproportionate to its cotton mills and posed a war-production risk. He supports an industry sized for roughly three million spindles and controlled through iron and steel supply.

subfiles.title: Offer of additional West letter copies
subfiles.about: West offers copies of his machinery policy letter for circulation.
subfiles.summary: Offers a dozen or more additional copies.

subfiles.title: State response to machinery industry proposals
subfiles.about: State explains its approach to limiting Japan’s industrial war potential.
subfiles.summary: Martin says iron, steel and machine-tool controls should constrain textile machinery expansion.

subfiles.title: Substitution on Turkish purchasing commission
subfiles.about: Turkey substitutes Ismail Kavadar for Nazif Inan.
subfiles.summary: Inan will remain in the United States; Kavadar will accompany the commission.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Turkish entry clearance
subfiles.about: Officials learn SCAP has granted entry and requests Circular 8 information.
subfiles.summary: Wolberg revises a letter to Millett accordingly.

subfiles.title: Turkish commission meeting and travel requirements
subfiles.about: Kavadar and Aydinelli provide required details and discuss travel timing.
subfiles.summary: They seek April entry before a mid-May shipment and ask about baggage. Officials also explain U.S. re-entry visa requirements for each commission member.

subfiles.title: Records check on Kavadar
subfiles.about: Department offices check Kavadar’s background.
subfiles.summary: The checks disclose no adverse information.

subfiles.title: Request for revised Turkish travel clearance
subfiles.about: State asks Joint Chiefs to clear Kavadar in place of Inan.
subfiles.summary: Hunt forwards required traveler statements and classified information about Sipahi, notes the May shipment deadline, and asks about baggage limits.

subfiles.title: Ragip Sipahi travel statement
subfiles.about: Provides Sipahi’s identity, itinerary and passport details.
subfiles.summary: Lists Sipahi’s textile mill role and proposed eight-month stay.

subfiles.title: Cevdet Aydinelli travel statement
subfiles.about: Provides Aydinelli’s identity, itinerary and passport details.
subfiles.summary: Lists his ministry role and proposed eight-month stay.

subfiles.title: Ismail N. Kavadar travel statement
subfiles.about: Provides Kavadar’s identity, itinerary and passport details.
subfiles.summary: Lists his commercial attaché role and proposed one-month stay.

subfiles.title: Draft reply to Turkish Embassy on commission change
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Turkey’s original commission request and Kavadar’s substitution.
subfiles.summary: The note begins acknowledgment of the March and April embassy notes; it continues beyond this section.
